1	# AI Insights
     2	
     3	A toolkit for structured, multi-agent AI development workflows. It gives AI coding agents a shared memory, a defined set of roles, and a headless execution path — so complex projects can be tackled across multiple chat sessions without losing context.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## 🧩 Tools
     8	
     9	### Agent Personas
    10	
    11	Pre-built prompt files that assign a specific role to an AI agent in your IDE (VS Code / Claude Code). Two suites are available:
    12	
    13	| Suite | Description | Docs |
    14	|-------|-------------|------|
    15	| **Ledger-Enabled** | 9-stage workflow (Planner → PM → Developer → QA → Security Auditor → Reviewer → Release Engineer → Docs → Synthesis) backed by the MCP server for persistent state | [personas/ledger/README.md](personas/ledger/README.md) |
    16	| **Standalone** | Single-purpose agents with no MCP dependency — drop in and use | [personas/standalone/](personas/standalone/) |
    17	
    18	### Project Ledger MCP Server
    19	
    20	A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that gives agents structured, persistent project state. It exposes 20 tools for managing work packages, tracking progress, and coordinating handoffs — with atomic writes and schema validation to prevent data corruption.
    21	
    22	→ [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md)
    23	
    24	### Orchestrator
    25	
    26	A headless, IDE-free alternative to the ledger workflow. Built on **LangGraph** + **Deep Agents**, it runs the same MCP-server-backed pipeline entirely from the command line — useful for automation, CI pipelines, or working outside an AI IDE.
    27	
    28	→ [orchestrator/README.md](orchestrator/README.md)
    29	
    30	---
    31	
    32	## 🚀 Quick Start
    33	
    34	```bash
    35	node scripts/cli.js
    36	```
    37	
    38	This opens an interactive menu where you can set up the workspace, sync personas, launch the GUI, run the orchestrator, and more — all from one place.
    39	
    40	Or run the full setup non-interactively:
    41	
    42	```bash
    43	node scripts/cli.js setup --all
    44	```
    45	
    46	You can also run any task directly:
    47	
    48	```bash
    49	node scripts/cli.js sync-personas          # build + deploy personas to IDE
    50	node scripts/cli.js gui                    # launch MCP GUI dashboard
    51	node scripts/cli.js orchestrator plan.md  # run orchestrator pipeline
    52	node scripts/cli.js ctx-generate          # generate context documentation
    53	node scripts/cli.js check-versions        # verify changelog vs manifest versions
    54	node scripts/cli.js read-log               # tail and query orchestrator logs
    55	node scripts/cli.js kill-orchestrator      # terminate stale orchestrator processes
    56	node scripts/cli.js kill-orchestrator --depth 5  # scan only 5 log files for lock cleanup
    57	node scripts/cli.js help                  # list all commands, grouped by category
    58	```
    59	
    60	> Commands are grouped in the help output by category: **Setup & Configuration**, **Validation & Utilities**, **Personas**, **MCP Server**, and **Orchestrator**. `read-log` and `kill-orchestrator` are available via direct dispatch but are not listed in the interactive help.
    61	
    62	> **Prerequisites:** Node.js >= 18. Python 3.11+ is only required for the orchestrator component. The `cli-menu` repository must be cloned as a sibling directory — see [Workspace directory layout](#workspace-directory-layout).
    63	
    64	Full setup and options for each sub-project:
    65	- [personas/ledger/README.md](personas/ledger/README.md) — Persona workflow guide
    66	- [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md) — MCP server architecture and GUI
    67	- [orchestrator/README.md](orchestrator/README.md) — Orchestrator setup, CLI reference
    68	
    69	---
    70	
    71	## 🛠 Development
    72	
    73	### Workspace directory layout
    74	
    75	The root `package.json` references `@mistralys/cli-menu` via a local `file:` path:
    76	
    77	```json
    78	"@mistralys/cli-menu": "file:../cli-menu"
    79	```
    80	
    81	This requires the `cli-menu` repository to be cloned as a **sibling directory** alongside `ai-insights/`:
    82	
    83	```
    84	parent/
    85	├── ai-insights/   ← this repository
    86	└── cli-menu/      ← required sibling
    87	```
    88	
    89	Running `npm install` inside `ai-insights/` will fail if `../cli-menu` does not exist. Clone or place the repository at that path before running any install or build steps.
    90	
    91	> **After `@mistralys/cli-menu` is published to npm:** update the dependency in
    92	> `package.json` from `"file:../cli-menu"` to `"^0.1.0"`, then run `npm install`.
    93	> Once updated, the sibling `cli-menu/` directory is no longer required.
    94	
    95	### Install the pre-commit hook
    96	
    97	```bash
    98	node scripts/install-hooks.js
    99	```

1	# Project Ledger MCP Server
     2	
     3	**A Model Context Protocol server that keeps AI coding agents in sync across sessions**
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## What Is This?
     8	
     9	The **Project Ledger MCP Server** is a specialized backend service that manages persistent project state for multi-agent AI workflows. It acts as a "source of truth" that agents can read from and write to, ensuring that work progress, decisions, and context are preserved across chat sessions.
    10	
    11	Think of it as a **structured database for AI agents**, where each agent can:
    12	- Check what work has been completed
    13	- See what's currently in progress
    14	- Understand dependencies between tasks
    15	- Record their findings and observations
    16	- Coordinate handoffs to the next agent in the workflow
    17	
    18	---
    19	
    20	## Why Does This Exist?
    21	
    22	### The Problem
    23	
    24	When building complex features with AI agents across multiple sessions, you face these challenges:
    25	
    26	1. **Context Loss**: Each new chat session starts from scratch. Agents can't remember what happened before.
    27	2. **Duplicate Work**: Without coordination, agents might redo completed tasks or miss dependencies.
    28	3. **Inconsistent State**: Manual JSON editing leads to typos, schema violations, and file corruption.
    29	4. **Race Conditions**: Multiple agents editing the same files simultaneously can cause conflicts.
    30	
    31	### The Solution
    32	
    33	The MCP server solves these problems by:
    34	
    35	- **Persisting State**: Maintains a structured JSON ledger on disk that survives between sessions
    36	- **Enforcing Validation**: Uses strict schemas (Zod) to prevent invalid data from being written
    37	- **Preventing Corruption**: Uses atomic writes and file locking to ensure data consistency
    38	- **Providing Coordination**: Offers workflow tools that tell agents what to do next based on project state
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## How It Works
    43	
    44	### Architecture
    45	
    46	The server exposes **22 MCP tools** that agents invoke to manage project state:
    47	
    48	```
    49	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    50	│          AI Agent (Developer/QA/etc.)           │
    51	└──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
    52	                   │ MCP Protocol (STDIO)
    53	                   │
    54	┌──────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
    55	│         Project Ledger MCP Server               │
    56	│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
    57	│  │  Tools: create_work_package,            │    │
    58	│  │         start_pipeline,                 │    │
    59	│  │         get_next_action, etc.           │    │
    60	│  └─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘    │
    61	│                    │                            │
    62	│  ┌─────────────────▼───────────────────────┐    │
    63	│  │  LedgerStore: Atomic I/O + Validation   │    │
    64	│  └─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘    │
    65	└────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┘
    66	                     │
    67	         ┌───────────┴──────────┐
    68	         │   JSON Files on Disk │
    69	         ├──────────────────────┤
    70	         │ storage/ledger/      │
    71	         │   {slug}/             │ ← Per-project subfolder
    72	         │     .meta.json        │ ← Project metadata
    73	         │     project-ledger.json│ ← Root index
    74	         │     WP-001.json       │ ← Work package 1
    75	         │     WP-002.json       │ ← Work package 2
    76	         │     plan.md           │ ← Archived plan document
    77	         │     synthesis.md      │ ← Archived synthesis report
    78	         │     orchestrator/     │
    79	         │       dialogues/      │ ← Agent dialogue capture (.md)
    80	         │       chunks/         │ ← Streaming chunk capture (.jsonl)
    81	         │     ...               │
    82	         └──────────────────────┘
    83	```
    84	
    85	> Ledger files are stored at `{mcp-server}/storage/ledger/{slug}/`, **not** inside plan folders.
    86	> Plan folders remain purely human-readable Markdown. Use `ledger_list_projects` to enumerate all tracked projects.
    87	
    88	### Data Model
    89	
    90	The server manages three types of files, all stored under the centralized ledger root:
    91	
    92	1. **Project Metadata** (`storage/ledger/{slug}/.meta.json`): Lightweight per-project summary
    93	   - Slug, original plan path, current status, timestamps
    94	   - Written automatically whenever the root index is updated
    95	   - Used by `ledger_list_projects` to enumerate all projects without loading full root indexes
    96	
    97	2. **Root Index** (`storage/ledger/{slug}/project-ledger.json`): High-level project metadata
    98	   - Project status (READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, BLOCKED)
    99	   - Work package summaries (status, assigned agent, dependencies)
   100	   - Project-level comments and incidents

   105	   - Acceptance criteria and completion status
   106	   - Pipeline history (implementation, QA, review, documentation)
   107	   - Artifacts (files modified, commit hashes, test results)
   108	   - Observations and technical debt notes
   109	
   110	4. **Orchestrator Capture Files** (`storage/ledger/{slug}/orchestrator/`): Files written by the orchestrator during a run
   111	   - `orchestrator/dialogues/` — Agent dialogue files (`{WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.md`), written by `write_dialogue()`; served by `handleListDialogues` / `handleGetDialogueFile`
   112	   - `orchestrator/chunks/` — Streaming chunk capture files (`{WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.jsonl`), written by `ChunkWriter`; served by `handleListChunks` / `handleGetChunkFile`
   113	
   114	5. **Archived Documents** (`storage/ledger/{slug}/plan.md`, `synthesis.md`): Read-only snapshots of key project documents
   115	   - `plan.md` — copied from the project folder when `ledger_initialize_project` is called
   116	   - `synthesis.md` — copied when `ledger_complete_synthesis` is called
   117	   - Both are served as formatted HTML by the GUI (`#/projects/:slug/plan` and `#/projects/:slug/synthesis`)
   118	   - Copies are best-effort; each tool response includes `archived_documents[]` and, when relevant, `archive_skipped[]`
   119	
   120	All four file types are kept in sync automatically — when an agent updates a work package, the server updates both JSON files and the `.meta.json` in a single atomic operation.
   121	
   122	---
   123	
   124	## Setup
   125	
   126	### Prerequisites
   127	
   128	- **Node.js** (ESM-compatible version)
   129	- **npm** or compatible package manager
   130	
   131	### Installation
   132	
   133	1. **Install dependencies**:
   134	   ```bash
   135	   cd mcp-server
   136	   npm install
   137	   ```
   138	
   139	2. **Configure Claude Desktop or Claude Code**:
   140	   
   141	   Add the server to your `.mcp.json` (or MCP configuration file):
   142	
   143	   ```json
   144	   {
   145	     "mcpServers": {
   146	       "project-ledger": {
   147	         "command": "npx",
   148	         "args": ["tsx", "/absolute/path/to/ai-insights/mcp-server/src/index.ts"]
   149	       }
   150	     }
   151	   }
   152	   ```
   153	
   154	   **Important**: Use the **absolute path** to the `src/index.ts` file on your system.
   155	
   156	   **Optional: Custom agents directory**
   157	
   158	   To enable auto-handoff, the server needs to locate your `*.agent.md` persona files. By default it auto-detects the VS Code User prompts folder for the current platform:
   159	
   160	   | Platform | Default path |
   161	   |---|---|
   162	   | macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/prompts/` |
   163	   | Linux | `~/.config/Code/User/prompts/` |
   164	   | Windows | `%APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts/` |
   165	
   166	   If your persona files live elsewhere, pass `--agents-dir` explicitly:
   167	
   168	   ```json
   169	   {
   170	     "mcpServers": {
   171	       "project-ledger": {
   172	         "command": "npx",
   173	         "args": [
   174	           "tsx",
   175	           "/absolute/path/to/ai-insights/mcp-server/src/index.ts",
   176	           "--agents-dir",
   177	           "/absolute/path/to/your/prompts"
   178	         ]
   179	       }
   180	     }
   181	   }
   182	   ```
   183	
   184	   If the directory is missing or contains no `*.agent.md` files, the server logs a warning and starts normally — auto-handoff is disabled but all other tools continue to work.
   185	
   186	3. **Restart your AI IDE** to load the MCP server
   187	
   188	4. **Verify**:
   189	   - The server starts automatically when Claude Code/Desktop launches
   190	   - Agents will perform a pre-flight check (`ledger_get_project_status`) before starting work
   191	   - If the server is unreachable, agents will report configuration errors
   192	   - On startup, the server logs agent discovery results to stderr:
   193	     - ✅ Success: `[project-ledger-mcp] Agent registry: 9 agents discovered from /path/to/prompts`
   194	     - ⚠️ Not found: `[project-ledger-mcp] agents_dir not found: /path. Auto-handoff disabled.`
   195	
   196	---
   197	
   198	## Usage
   199	
   200	### For Agent Workflows
   201	
   202	The MCP server is designed to work with the [Ledger-Enabled Agent Workflow](../personas/ledger/README.md). Agents use the server automatically — you don't need to invoke tools manually.
   203	
   204	**Typical Agent Session:**
   205	
   206	1. **Agent checks project status** via `ledger_get_project_status`
   207	2. **Agent reads work package details** via `ledger_get_work_package`
   208	3. **Agent performs work** (writes code, runs tests, etc.)
   209	4. **Agent updates ledger** via MCP tools:
   210	   - `ledger_start_pipeline` — Begins implementation/QA/review
   211	   - `ledger_complete_pipeline` — Records results and artifacts
   212	   - `ledger_add_observation` — Notes technical debt or improvements
   213	   - `ledger_update_work_package_status` — Marks tasks complete
   214	
   215	5. **Agent asks for next action** via `ledger_get_next_action` or `ledger_get_handoff_status`
   216	
   217	   `ledger_get_handoff_status` may return an `auto_handoff` object:
   218	   ```json
   219	   {
   220	     "current_agent": "Developer",
   221	     "next_agent": "QA",
   222	     "status": "HANDOFF",
   223	     "auto_handoff": {
   224	       "agent_name": "4 - QA v3.6.1",
   225	       "agent_id": "ledger-4-qa",
   226	       "cc_agent_name": "4-qa",
   227	       "vs_agent_name": "4 - QA v3.6.1",
   228	       "da_agent_name": "4-qa",
   229	       "prompt": "@ledger-4-qa\nProject path: /path/to/plan"
   230	     }
   231	   }
   232	   ```
   233	   When present, the IDE can invoke the next agent automatically without human routing. When absent, use the standard `CURRENT AGENT / NEXT AGENT / STATUS` block for manual routing.
   234	
   235	### Example: Developer Agent Flow
   236	
   237	```
   238	User: "Implement WP-003"
   239	
   240	Agent:
   241	1. Calls ledger_get_work_package(WP-003)
   242	   └─ Reads: Acceptance criteria, dependencies, current status
   243	
   244	2. Validates dependencies are complete
   245	
   246	3. Calls ledger_claim_work_package(WP-003, agent="Developer")
   247	   └─ Updates: Status READY → IN_PROGRESS
   248	
   249	4. Calls ledger_start_pipeline(type="implementation")
   250	   └─ Creates: New pipeline entry with status IN_PROGRESS
   251	
   252	5. Implements the feature (writes code)
   253	
   254	6. Calls ledger_complete_pipeline(
   255	     status="PASS",
   256	     summary=["Added authentication middleware", "Updated routes"],
   257	     artifacts={files_modified: ["src/auth.ts", "src/routes.ts"]},
   258	     acceptance_criteria_updates=[{criterion: "Auth required", met: true}]
   259	   )
   260	   └─ Updates: Pipeline status, artifacts, acceptance criteria
   261	
   262	7. After QA, review, and documentation pipelines pass, the Documentation Agent calls
   263	   ledger_update_work_package_status(status="COMPLETE", agent="Documentation Agent")
   264	   └─ Updates: WP-003 status to COMPLETE (if all criteria met)
   265	```
   266	
   267	### For Manual Inspection
   268	
   269	You can read the ledger files directly — they're human-readable JSON:
   270	
   271	```bash
   272	# View project overview
   273	cat storage/ledger/2026-02-11-feature-name/project-ledger.json
   274	
   275	# View work package details
   276	cat storage/ledger/2026-02-11-feature-name/WP-001.json
   277	
   278	# View project metadata
   279	cat storage/ledger/2026-02-11-feature-name/.meta.json
   280	```
   281	
   282	**Warning**: Never edit ledger files manually. Always let agents use MCP tools to ensure consistency.
   283	
   284	---
   285	
   286	## GUI Dashboard
   287	
   288	A lightweight web dashboard for monitoring and managing projects tracked in the ledger.
   289	
   290	**Start the GUI server:**
   291	```sh
   292	npm run gui
   293	```
   294	Then open [http://localhost:3420](http://localhost:3420) in your browser.
   295	
   296	**Custom port or ledger directory:**
   297	```sh
   298	npx tsx gui/server.ts --port 4000 --ledger-dir /path/to/ledger
   299	```

   319	- Browse all project comments across every project on the **Insights page** (`#/insights`) — filter by type, priority, or project; auto-refreshes every 15 seconds
   320	- **Orchestrator view** (`#/orchestrator`) — launch and monitor orchestrator runs from the GUI: enter an absolute path to a `plan.md`, click **Run Preflight** to validate environment readiness (renders a pass/fail checklist per check), then click **Start Run** (enabled only when all preflight checks pass) to launch a run; after a successful launch a confirmation banner is shown in the preflight results area — the banner is **automatically cleared** once the Run Queue renders with at least one entry (only the success banner is cleared; error banners are intentionally left intact); a live **Run Queue** table polls every 5 seconds and shows each entry's status badge, elapsed time, and progress summary; rows are expandable for an inline log preview; pending entries show a Kill button, dead entries show a Dismiss button, and started entries link to their project detail page; a **CLI Reference** card at the bottom lists the equivalent shell commands; the view is reachable from the top nav bar and via direct URL (`#/orchestrator`)

   326	
   327	> The GUI server is a **separate process** from the MCP server. Both can run simultaneously and share the same ledger directory. The MCP server monitors `gui-config.json` for configuration changes via `fs.watch()` — changes take effect immediately without restarting.
   328	
   329	### GUI Backend Modules
   330	
   331	The GUI backend is composed of focused utility modules in `src/gui/`:
   332	
   333	| Module | Purpose |
   334	|--------|---------|
   335	| `config.ts` | Reads and watches `gui-config.json`; exposes typed configuration to the API layer |
   336	| `auto-archive.ts` | Background job that auto-archives completed projects after a configurable delay |
   337	| `log-resolver.ts` | Locates and reads orchestrator run log files (JSONL); provides `resolveOrchestratorLogsDir`, `findRunLogs`, and `readLogEntries` — see below |
   338	| `api.ts` (dialogue handlers) | `handleListDialogues` and `handleGetDialogueFile` serve the project's `orchestrator/dialogues/` directory — see below |
   339	| `api.ts` (chunk handlers) | `handleListChunks` and `handleGetChunkFile` serve the project's `orchestrator/chunks/` directory — see below |
   340	| `chunk-renderer.ts` | Pure JSONL-to-Markdown renderer; exports `renderChunksToMarkdown(jsonlContent: string): string` — no I/O, no side effects; powers the `/chunks/:filename/rendered` endpoint — see below |
   341	
   342	#### `log-resolver.ts` — Orchestrator Run Log Resolver
   343	
   344	Provides three exported functions for reading orchestrator run logs:
   345	
   346	- **`resolveOrchestratorLogsDir(configured: string | undefined): string`** — Returns `configured` if it is a non-empty string; otherwise falls back to `~/.ai-insights/orchestrator-logs`.
   347	- **`findRunLogs(logsDir: string, slug: string): Promise<string[]>`** — Lists files in `logsDir` whose names match `<prefix>-{slug}.jsonl`. Files without a non-empty prefix are excluded. Returns an empty array when the directory does not exist.
   348	- **`readLogEntries(logsDir: string, filename: string, afterLine?: number): Promise<{ entries: unknown[]; totalLines: number }>`** — Reads and parses a JSONL log file. Malformed lines are silently skipped. `totalLines` always reflects the full line count; `entries` contains parsed objects from line `afterLine + 1` onward.
   349	
   350	**Security:** `readLogEntries` enforces a dual-layer path-traversal defence:
   351	1. **Filename allowlist** — rejects any filename that contains `..`, `/`, or characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.
   352	2. **Resolved-path escape check** — `path.resolve()` verifies the resolved path stays within `logsDir`, preventing CWD-relative or symlink escapes.
   353	
   354	Both layers throw `ApiError FORBIDDEN` on violation. Errors are written to **stderr only** (STDIO discipline preserved).
   355	
   356	> **Known limitation:** `resolveOrchestratorLogsDir` and `findRunLogs` do not currently validate that the supplied path is absolute. If a relative path is stored in `gui-config.json`, `findRunLogs` may resolve it against the process CWD. `readLogEntries` is immune to this (its escape-check uses `path.resolve()`). A `path.isAbsolute()` guard is planned before these functions are wired into any HTTP-facing endpoint.
   357	
   358	#### Dialogue API handlers — `GET /api/projects/:slug/dialogues[?wp=WP-001]` and `GET /api/projects/:slug/dialogues/:filename`
   359	
   360	Two API handlers in `gui/api.ts` expose the agent dialogue files written by the orchestrator's dialogue capture feature:
   361	
   362	- **`handleListDialogues(ledgerRoot, slug, wpId?): Promise<DialogueEntry[]>`** — Returns a sorted array of `DialogueEntry` objects (`{ filename, wp_id, stage }`) from `storage/ledger/{slug}/orchestrator/dialogues/`. Returns `[]` when the directory is absent (no error thrown). The `wp_id` and `stage` fields are parsed from the filename convention `{WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.md`; filenames that do not match the convention produce empty strings for those fields. Optional `wpId` argument filters to filenames that start with `{wpId}-` (e.g. `'WP-001'` returns only `WP-001-*.md` files).
   363	- **`handleGetDialogueFile(ledgerRoot, slug, filename): Promise<string>`** — Returns the raw Markdown content of a single dialogue file. Throws `ApiError NOT_FOUND` when the filename is rejected by the allowlist or the file does not exist.
   364	
   365	**Security:** `handleGetDialogueFile` enforces a dual-layer path-traversal defence identical in structure to `readLogEntries`:
   366	1. **Filename allowlist** — `DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/` rejects any filename containing `.`, `/`, or other special characters. The `filename` path segment is decoded with `decodeURIComponent()` in `server.ts` before the check, so percent-encoded traversals (e.g. `%2E%2E%2Fsecret.md`) are also rejected.
   367	2. **Resolved-path escape check** — `path.resolve()` verifies the resolved file path stays within the project's `orchestrator/dialogues/` directory.
   368	
   369	Both layers throw `ApiError NOT_FOUND` on violation (no leaking of filesystem layout).
   370	
   371	#### GUI Frontend — Dialogues card (`views/work-package.js`)
   372	
   373	The WP Detail view includes a **Dialogues card** rendered asynchronously after the Handoff Notes section. Two new methods on the `API` object (in `api-client.js`) back this feature:
   374	
   375	- **`API.getDialogues(slug, wpId)`** — `GET /api/projects/:slug/dialogues?wp={wpId}`. Returns a parsed JSON array of `{ filename, stage, wp_id }` objects. Hand-rolls its `?wp=` query string (consistent with `getRunLogEntries`).
   376	- **`API.getDialogueContent(slug, filename)`** — `GET /api/projects/:slug/dialogues/:filename`. Returns raw Markdown text via `res.text()`. Uses a direct `fetch()` call rather than the internal `request()` helper, which calls `res.json()`.
   377	
   378	**Rendering flow:**
   379	
   380	1. A `<div id="wp-dialogues-section">` placeholder is injected synchronously into `app.innerHTML` at the bottom of the WP detail DOM (after `handoffHtml`). A closure reference (`dialoguesEl`) is captured before the async call resolves.
   381	2. `API.getDialogues()` is called. If the response is empty, a "No dialogues available" message is rendered in the placeholder.
   382	3. For a non-empty response, dialogues are grouped by `stage` (insertion order preserved). Each stage renders as a row with a label and pill buttons — one per revision (`stage-r0`, `stage-r1`, …). The last revision gets the `.dialogue-btn-latest` class (bold, blue-bordered).
   383	4. A single delegated `click` listener on `dialoguesEl` handles all button presses via `e.target.closest('.dialogue-btn')`.
   384	5. Clicking a button calls `API.getDialogueContent()` and renders the result with `marked.parse()` inside a `.dialogue-content` container. The output is set via `innerHTML` (trusted HTML — consistent with plan/synthesis rendering; no sanitization).
   385	6. An `activeBtn` closure variable tracks the currently expanded button for collapse/toggle behaviour: clicking a different button collapses the current one; clicking the same button again toggles it off.
   386	7. `getDialogueContent` errors render an inline `.text-danger` message. `getDialogues` errors render a `.text-danger` message inside the Dialogues card. Neither error propagates to the surrounding WP view.
   387	
   388	> **Accessibility (future):** `.dialogue-btn` buttons do not set `aria-expanded`. A future pass should toggle it alongside `.dialogue-btn-active`.
   389	
   390	#### Chunk API handlers — `GET /api/projects/:slug/chunks[?wp=WP-001]` and `GET /api/projects/:slug/chunks/:filename`
   391	
   392	Two API handlers in `gui/api.ts` expose the streaming chunk files written by the orchestrator's `ChunkWriter`. They mirror the dialogue handlers exactly, differing only in directory path and file extension.
   393	
   394	**Exported types:**
   395	
   396	```typescript
   397	interface ChunkEntry {
   398	  filename: string;  // e.g. 'WP-001-implementation-r0.jsonl'
   399	  wp_id:    string;  // e.g. 'WP-001' (empty string when filename does not match the convention)
   400	  stage:    string;  // e.g. 'implementation' (empty string when filename does not match)
   401	}
   402	```
   403	
   404	**Handlers:**
   405	
   406	- **`handleListChunks(ledgerRoot, slug, wpId?): Promise<ChunkEntry[]>`** — Returns a sorted array of `ChunkEntry` objects from `storage/ledger/{slug}/orchestrator/chunks/`. Returns `[]` when the directory is absent (ENOENT/ENOTDIR), with no error thrown. The `wp_id` and `stage` fields are parsed from the filename convention `{WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.jsonl`; filenames that do not match the convention produce empty strings for those fields. The optional `wpId` argument must match `WP_ID_RE = /^WP-\d+$/`; invalid values (e.g. injection attempts) silently return `[]` rather than an error. When valid, only filenames starting with `{wpId}-` are returned.
   407	
   408	- **`handleGetChunkFile(ledgerRoot, slug, filename): Promise<{ content: string }>`** — Returns the raw JSONL content of a single chunk file. Throws `ApiError NOT_FOUND` (404) when the filename is rejected by the allowlist or the file does not exist.
   409	
   410	**Security:** `handleGetChunkFile` enforces the same dual-layer path-traversal defence as `handleGetDialogueFile`:
   411	1. **Filename allowlist** — `CHUNK_FILENAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/` rejects any filename containing `.`, `/`, spaces, or other special characters (including `..` traversal attempts).
   412	2. **Resolved-path escape check** — `path.resolve()` verifies the resolved file path stays inside the project's `orchestrator/chunks/` directory (defence-in-depth against symlink and encoding escapes).
   413	
   414	Both layers throw `ApiError NOT_FOUND` on violation. Rejection events are written to `console.warn` (stderr only — STDIO discipline preserved).
   415	
   416	**Cross-language coupling:** `CHUNKS_DIR = 'orchestrator/chunks' as const` (exported from `src/utils/constants.ts`) must exactly match the path used by the Python orchestrator's `ChunkWriter`. Changing either side without updating the other will break chunk file discovery.
   417	
   418	#### `chunk-renderer.ts` — JSONL-to-Markdown renderer
   419	
   420	A pure TypeScript module (no I/O, no side effects) that converts a raw JSONL chunk file into rendered Markdown. Imported directly by `server.ts` to back the `/rendered` endpoint — there is no separate HTTP handler; the composition happens inline in the route dispatcher:
   421	
   422	```typescript
   423	handleGetChunkFile(ledgerRoot, slug, filename).then(({ content }) => ({
   424	  content: renderChunksToMarkdown(content),
   425	}))
   426	```
   427	
   428	**Public API:**
   429	
   430	- **`renderChunksToMarkdown(jsonlContent: string): string`** — Parses a JSONL chunk file produced by the Python `ChunkWriter`, merges token-level `AIMessageChunk` data into complete messages (accumulating `content`, `tool_calls`, and `usage_metadata`), groups messages by namespace (main agent first, then sub-agents under `### Subagent:` headings), and renders Markdown consistent with the orchestrator's `serialize_messages_to_markdown()` output format.
   431	
   432	**JSONL format (chunk_format: 1):**
   433	
   434	Each file begins with a header line (`{"chunk_format": 1, ...}`) followed by one event per line. Events may arrive in two equivalent wire shapes:
   435	- **Object shape:** `{"ns": namespace, "msg": AIMessageChunk.model_dump(), "metadata": {...}}`
   436	- **Array shape:** `[namespace, AIMessageChunk.model_dump(), metadata]`
   437	
   438	Both shapes are normalised to a common internal representation before processing.
   439	
   440	**Routing:** `GET /api/projects/:slug/chunks/:filename/rendered`
   441	- `rest.length === 5`, `rest[2] === 'chunks'`, `rest[4] === 'rendered'`
   442	- Placed before the `/:filename` route (rest.length 4) in `server.ts` for visual grouping; because the two routes have *different* `rest.length` values, the dispatcher can never confuse them — placement is purely cosmetic.
   443	- Returns `{ content: string }` — the rendered Markdown string.
   444	- Inherits all security guards from `handleGetChunkFile` (CHUNK_FILENAME_RE allowlist + path-prefix escape check).
   445	
   446	#### GUI Frontend — Chunks card (`views/work-package.js`)
   447	
   448	The WP Detail view's **Dialogues card** was updated in WP-006 to prefer streaming chunk files over Markdown dialogue files. Two new methods on the `API` object (in `api-client.js`) back the chunk path:
   449	
   450	- **`API.getChunks(slug, wpId)`** — `GET /api/projects/:slug/chunks?wp={wpId}`. Returns a parsed JSON array of `{ filename, stage, wp_id }` objects (`ChunkEntry[]`). Always appends `?wp=`, consistent with `getDialogues`.
   451	- **`API.getChunkRendered(slug, filename)`** — `GET /api/projects/:slug/chunks/{filename}/rendered`. Returns rendered Markdown text via `data.content` (JSON unwrap, same pattern as `getDialogueContent`).
   452	
   453	**Chunk-first rendering flow:**
   454	
   455	1. `renderWorkPackageDetail()` issues `Promise.all([API.getChunks(...).catch(() => []), API.getDialogues(...)])` in parallel. The `catch` on `getChunks` silently swallows errors (absent `chunks/` directory is expected for older runs that predate streaming capture).
   456	2. When `chunks.length > 0`, `useChunks = true` and `entries = chunks`; otherwise `entries = dialogues` (fallback path).
   457	3. Each entry button receives `data-use-chunks="1"` (chunk path) or `data-use-chunks="0"` (dialogue path). The `click` listener reads this attribute and calls `API.getChunkRendered()` or `API.getDialogueContent()` accordingly.
   458	4. The rendered Markdown is parsed with `marked.parse()` and injected into `.dialogue-content` as HTML. Error handling follows the same inline `.text-danger` pattern as the dialogue path.
   459	
   460	> **Backward compatibility:** Projects created before the streaming capture feature have no `orchestrator/chunks/` directory. The silent `catch(() => [])` on `getChunks` ensures these projects fall back cleanly to the existing Markdown dialogue display with no UI change.
   461	
   462	#### GUI Frontend — Knowledge API client methods (`api-client.js`)
   463	
   464	Five methods on the `API` object (in `api-client.js`) back the Knowledge page (`#/knowledge`). All five encode the insight `id` path segment via `encodeURIComponent` and follow the same `request()` helper pattern as every other API client method.
   465	
   466	- **`API.getKnowledge(params)`** — `GET /api/knowledge[?scope=…&project_slug=…&…]`. Returns a parsed JSON response listing or searching knowledge insights. Builds the query string via `buildQueryString`; falsy/empty param values are silently omitted — pass `undefined` to leave a filter unset rather than sending `?key=undefined` to the server.
   467	
   468	- **`API.updateKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug, data)`** — `PATCH /api/knowledge/:id`. Merges `scope` and `project_slug` into the JSON body **after** the caller-supplied `data` object (`Object.assign({}, data, { scope, project_slug })`), so scope/slug always take precedence over same-named keys in `data`. A falsy `projectSlug` (empty string, `null`, `undefined`) is coerced to `undefined` and omitted from JSON serialisation.
   469	
   470	- **`API.deleteKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug)`** — `DELETE /api/knowledge/:id?scope=…[&project_slug=…]`. Passes scope/slug as URL query parameters so the server can locate the correct store file. A falsy `projectSlug` is omitted from the query string by `buildQueryString`.
   471	
   472	- **`API.promoteKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug)`** — `POST /api/knowledge/:id/promote?scope=…[&project_slug=…]`. **Sends no request body** — the server identifies the source insight via the query parameters alone. Returns the newly created global insight (which receives a new ID from the global store's `next_id` counter, different from the original project insight ID).
   473	
   474	- **`API.moveKnowledge(id, sourceScope, sourceProjectSlug, targetProjectSlug)`** — `POST /api/knowledge/:id/move`. Sends `source_scope`, `source_project_slug` (omitted when falsy — global-scope moves have no source project slug), and `project_slug` (the target; always required, never coerced) in the JSON body. Returns the newly created insight in the target project (with a new ID from the target store).
   475	
   476	**Coercion rule:** All four mutating methods (`updateKnowledge`, `deleteKnowledge`, `promoteKnowledge`, `moveKnowledge`) use `projectSlug || undefined` to drop falsy slugs. This is safe in practice because project slugs are always non-empty strings — the only exception is `moveKnowledge`'s `targetProjectSlug`, which is intentionally **not** coerced because a move always requires an explicit destination.
   477	
   478	---
   479	
   480	## Available Tools
   481	
   482	The server exposes 22 MCP tools organized by category:
   483	
   484	### Project Lifecycle
   485	- `ledger_get_project_status` — Read project overview
   486	- `ledger_initialize_project` — Create new ledger
   487	- `ledger_list_projects` — List all tracked projects (optionally filter by status)
   488	- `ledger_detect_project` — Auto-detect project from a workspace path
   489	- `ledger_complete_synthesis` — Mark synthesis as generated; transitions project to COMPLETE if all WPs are done
   490	
   491	### Work Packages
   492	- `ledger_get_work_package` — Read full WP details
   493	- `ledger_list_work_packages` — List/filter work packages
   494	- `ledger_create_work_package` — Create new work package
   495	- `ledger_claim_work_package` — Start working on a WP
   496	- `ledger_update_work_package_status` — Update WP status

461	
   462	#### GUI Frontend — Knowledge API client methods (`api-client.js`)
   463	
   464	Five methods on the `API` object (in `api-client.js`) back the Knowledge page (`#/knowledge`). All five encode the insight `id` path segment via `encodeURIComponent` and follow the same `request()` helper pattern as every other API client method.
   465	
   466	- **`API.getKnowledge(params)`** — `GET /api/knowledge[?scope=…&project_slug=…&…]`. Returns a parsed JSON response listing or searching knowledge insights. Builds the query string via `buildQueryString`; falsy/empty param values are silently omitted — pass `undefined` to leave a filter unset rather than sending `?key=undefined` to the server.
   467	
   468	- **`API.updateKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug, data)`** — `PATCH /api/knowledge/:id`. Merges `scope` and `project_slug` into the JSON body **after** the caller-supplied `data` object (`Object.assign({}, data, { scope, project_slug })`), so scope/slug always take precedence over same-named keys in `data`. A falsy `projectSlug` (empty string, `null`, `undefined`) is coerced to `undefined` and omitted from JSON serialisation.
   469	
   470	- **`API.deleteKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug)`** — `DELETE /api/knowledge/:id?scope=…[&project_slug=…]`. Passes scope/slug as URL query parameters so the server can locate the correct store file. A falsy `projectSlug` is omitted from the query string by `buildQueryString`.
   471	
   472	- **`API.promoteKnowledge(id, scope, projectSlug)`** — `POST /api/knowledge/:id/promote?scope=…[&project_slug=…]`. **Sends no request body** — the server identifies the source insight via the query parameters alone. Returns the newly created global insight (which receives a new ID from the global store's `next_id` counter, different from the original project insight ID).
   473	
   474	- **`API.moveKnowledge(id, sourceScope, sourceProjectSlug, targetProjectSlug)`** — `POST /api/knowledge/:id/move`. Sends `source_scope`, `source_project_slug` (omitted when falsy — global-scope moves have no source project slug), and `project_slug` (the target; always required, never coerced) in the JSON body. Returns the newly created insight in the target project (with a new ID from the target store).
   475	
   476	**Coercion rule:** All four mutating methods (`updateKnowledge`, `deleteKnowledge`, `promoteKnowledge`, `moveKnowledge`) use `projectSlug || undefined` to drop falsy slugs. This is safe in practice because project slugs are always non-empty strings — the only exception is `moveKnowledge`'s `targetProjectSlug`, which is intentionally **not** coerced because a move always requires an explicit destination.
   477	
   478	---
   479	
   480	## Available Tools
   481	
   482	The server exposes 22 MCP tools organized by category:
   483	
   484	### Project Lifecycle
   485	- `ledger_get_project_status` — Read project overview
   486	- `ledger_initialize_project` — Create new ledger
   487	- `ledger_list_projects` — List all tracked projects (optionally filter by status)
   488	- `ledger_detect_project` — Auto-detect project from a workspace path
   489	- `ledger_complete_synthesis` — Mark synthesis as generated; transitions project to COMPLETE if all WPs are done
   490	
   491	### Work Packages
   492	- `ledger_get_work_package` — Read full WP details
   493	- `ledger_list_work_packages` — List/filter work packages
   494	- `ledger_create_work_package` — Create new work package
   495	- `ledger_claim_work_package` — Start working on a WP
   496	- `ledger_update_work_package_status` — Update WP status
   497	- `ledger_reset_rework_count` — Reset rework counter for a pipeline type on a WP (PM-only)
   498	- `ledger_update_acceptance_criteria` — Add, remove, or modify acceptance criteria on a WP (PM-only)
   499	
   500	### Pipelines
   501	- `ledger_begin_work` — Claim a READY WP and start its pipeline in a single atomic call (replaces `ledger_claim_work_package` + `ledger_start_pipeline` two-step)
   502	- `ledger_start_pipeline` — Begin implementation/QA/review/docs phase
   503	- `ledger_complete_pipeline` — Record results and artifacts
   504	- `ledger_cancel_pipeline` — Cancel a stale IN_PROGRESS pipeline (marks it FAIL)
   505	- `ledger_update_pipeline_progress` — Update summary of an IN_PROGRESS pipeline without completing it
   506	
   507	### Observations
   508	- `ledger_add_observation` — Add comment to pipeline
   509	- `ledger_add_project_comment` — Add project-level comment
   510	
   511	### Workflow Coordination
   512	- `ledger_get_next_action` — Ask "what should I do next?" (includes stale pipeline detection); pass `max_results` to get up to N actionable WPs in one call
   513	- `ledger_get_handoff_status` — Compute handoff status for current agent
   514	
   515	### Help & Documentation
   516	- `ledger_help` — Get usage documentation, examples, and required parameters for all tools (pass no args for overview, or `tool_name` for a specific tool)
   517	
   518	For detailed API signatures and parameters, see the [API Surface](docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md).
   519	
   520	---
   521	
   522	## Key Features
   523	
   524	### ✅ Atomic Operations
   525	
   526	All writes use the **write-to-temp-then-rename** pattern:
   527	- Prevents readers from seeing partial writes
   528	- Ensures JSON files are never corrupted
   529	
   530	### ✅ File Locking
   531	
   532	Distributed file locking with `proper-lockfile`:
   533	- Prevents race conditions when multiple agents run concurrently
   534	- Automatic stale lock detection (10 second timeout)
   535	- Retry logic with exponential backoff
   536	
   537	### ✅ Schema Validation
   538	
   539	All data validated with Zod before reading or writing:
   540	- Catches schema violations early
   541	- TypeScript types inferred from schemas
   542	- Runtime validation on every I/O operation
   543	
   544	### ✅ Dual-File Sync
   545	
   546	Work package updates are atomic across both files:
   547	- Root index and WP detail always stay consistent
   548	- Single lock protects both files during update
   549	- No possibility of split-brain state
   550	
   551	### ✅ Agent Auto-Discovery
   552	
   553	At startup the server scans the configured agents directory for `*.agent.md` files:
   554	- Reads each file's front-matter to extract the agent role name
   555	- Populates an in-process registry used by `ledger_get_handoff_status` to route automatic handoffs
   556	- Controlled via `--agents-dir <path>` or platform-specific defaults (see [Setup](#setup))
   557	- If discovery fails or the directory is missing, auto-handoff is silently disabled and all other tools continue to work normally
   558	
   559	### ✅ Infinite-Loop Protection
